description_full: Iridium Communications Inc. provides mobile voice and data communications services and products to businesses, the United States and foreign governments, non-governmental organizations, and consumers in the United States, Canada, and internationally. The company offers mobile satellite communications services for land mobile end users and aviation sectors; broadband terminals, embedded devices, and handsets for merchant shipping, fishing, leisure and research vessels, and specialized watercraft; satellite-based IoT services; hosted payload and other data services; and other data services and engineering services. It also provides postpaid mobile voice and data satellite communications; prepaid mobile voice satellite communications; push-to-talk; broadband data; Internet of Things (IoT); and satellite time and location services. In addition, the company offers personnel tracking devices; asset tracking devices for equipment, vehicles, and aircrafts; beyond-line-of-sight aircraft communications applications; maritime communications applications; specialized communications solutions for high-value individuals; and mobile communications and data devices for the military and other government agencies, such as secure satellite handsets; and maintenance services for the U.S. government's dedicated gateway. Further, it provides satellite handsets, voice and data modems, broadband data devices, and IoT data devices; and various accessories for its devices that include batteries, holsters, earbud headphones, portable auxiliary antennas, antenna adaptors, USB data cables, and charging units. The company sells its products and services to commercial end users through a wholesale distribution network that includes service providers, and value-added resellers and value-added manufacturers. The company was formerly known as Iridium Holdings LLC and changed its name to Iridium Communications Inc. in September 2009. Iridium Communications Inc. is headquartered in McLean, Virginia.

financial_summary: Iridium Communications Inc is a mid-cap communication services business with a $4.7B market cap on $872M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years and +8% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 3% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $300M in free cash flow — roughly 34 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.50× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -11.3% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.7× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage of 16× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 5.3% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 12% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sect: Its 27% operating margin runs 18pp above the Communication Services median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.32x).
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+26.7% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.06 across 169 companies in the universe; the top four hold 36% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 196% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 13% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 23% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 60% and a beta of 0.82, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 1.88 vs 5y 0.70), so read it loosely.
About $39.8M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 44% in the 2020 crash, 22% in the 2022 bear market and 9% in 2008.
val: The stock trades only 5% below its DCF fair value of $46.26, a thin margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 20%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $25.42 to $82.41 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Communication Services peers: P/E 28.6 vs 14.9, EV/EBITDA 16.6 vs 9.4 and P/FCF 15.6 vs 11.3 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 60% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 6.4% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The 3 covering analysts target $48.00 on average, 9% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 3% falls short of the cost of capital of 7.6%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.76).
It converts 34% of revenue into free cash flow, or 28% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality is mixed: cash conversion of 3.50x, but high accruals (-11.3% of assets).
ROE of 25% is amplified by 5.5x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
Operating margin is running 11pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 2.3% of revenue on R&D and 5.9% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 3.7x net debt to EBITDA ($96.5M of cash against $1.8B of debt), with interest covered 16.1x.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 6.5% over 3 years, 8.4% over 5 years and 7.8% over 10 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 7.3% a year over five years.
Capex runs only 0.5x depreciation (11.5% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 37, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own 11.9%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 87%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (7 sales, net $13.3M sold).
It returns 5.3% a year to shareholders (4.0% in buybacks and 1.4% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 3.5% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 975 employees, each generates about $894K of revenue, 1.5x the Communication Services median, and productivity has risen 6.0% a year.
That works out to $307K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.4M (2x revenue per employee).
